tasks.description: In `orchestrator/mcp_tools.py:_handle_get_status()`, after building the status dict (~line 898), extract `phase_started_at` from `phase_data.get('started_at')` and compute `phase_elapsed_seconds` as `int((now - started_at).total_seconds())`. Add both to the status response. Guard against `None` by omitting fields when `started_at` is absent.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: get_status response includes phase_started_at (ISO 8601 string) and phase_elapsed_seconds (integer) when the current phase has a started_at value; fields are omitted when started_at is None

tasks.description: In the same method, after filtering running_agents (~line 904), iterate over each agent and add `elapsed_seconds` computed from `agent['started_at']`. Guard against missing/None started_at by skipping agents without it.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: Each running_agents entry includes elapsed_seconds (integer) when the agent has a started_at value; field is omitted when started_at is None

tasks.description: In `orchestrator/tests/test_mcp_tools.py`, update the `_pipeline_response` fixture to include `started_at` on the phase and agents. Add tests verifying phase_started_at, phase_elapsed_seconds, and per-agent elapsed_seconds appear correctly, and that they are omitted when started_at is None.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: Tests pass for both present and absent started_at cases

pr.title: Add server-computed timing fields to get_status response
pr.description:
Add phase_started_at, phase_elapsed_seconds, and per-agent elapsed_seconds
to the get_status MCP tool response. Server-computed timing eliminates
client-side wall-clock drift caused by blocking dialogs during monitoring.
pr.test_plan:
- Automated: unit tests in test_mcp_tools.py cover present/absent started_at cases
- Manual: run /sdlc --short on a test task and verify the status response includes timing fields
